name: Kimbundu
readall_conflicts: The one listed work could not be opened, so it contributes nothing. our files already held three files from the 2026-09-16 pass (no lines for them); two of them speak to Kimbundu stress and they pull in different directions. Chatelain 1889 (Pronuncia p. XXI-XXII, English and Portuguese columns): 'Accent: General rule: The accent falls on the penult. Ex.: ngitumáka. Exceptions are due: a) to contraction or abscission; thus: kiá from kiabu, bana from banau, b) to foreign origin, especially when the accent falls on the antepenult, c) to enclitic monosyllables, which attract the accent to the last syllable of the preceding word, thus, tunga 'nzo, pronounce: tunga'nzo.' / 'Accentuação: Regra geral: O accento tónico recahe sobre a penúltima' - this agrees with the catalog's penult rule and adds exceptions (oxytones from contraction, antepenult in loans, enclitics shifting accent to the host's final syllable). Xavier 2010 (USP dissertation 'Fonologia do quimbundo', PDF pp. 122 and 127 of the file): 'não penso que o acento tenha uma função distintiva em quimbundo, por se tratar, antes de tudo, de uma ocorrência secundária, isto é, ocasionada por questões de movimento do tom alto dentro de combinações de palavras. Com efeito, não existem pares mínimos fundados em um contraste acentual entre sílabas tônicas e sílabas átonas atestados em quimbundo' and, in the conclusion, 'O quimbundo não possui acento com função distintiva. O estudo realizado sobre a organização de seus supra-segmento…

audit.recode_to: tone-only / no word stress (catalog's 'no fixed stress; lexical-grammatical H/L tone' class). If the editor keeps a prominence coding, it must at minimum carry a caution + contra entry: 'Chatelain's penult accent = H of the prevalent H-L word-tone scheme; Xavier 2010 (instrumental, 5 spk) finds no stress and no penult lengthening'.
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote: no file was. I downloaded the cited archive.org fulltext and the English and Portuguese sentences are there verbatim at front-matter pp. xxi-xxiii, with the exceptions the record's cite line mentions. (2) Deciding source is an 1888-89 missionary 'grammatica elementar' whose accent rule predates tonal analysis; Chatelain himself (§192, p.153) already notices word-melody minimal pairs that are 'not tonic accent'. (3) The best available prosodic description, Xavier 2010 (USP PhD, 158 pp, Praat, 5 speakers from Luanda/Bengo/Cuanza Norte/Malanje), devotes §3.4 to 'the accentual question' and concludes Kimbundu is exclusively tonal (H, L), syllable-timed, with no vowel reduction, no stress ('inexistente em quimbundo'), and no lengthening other than V+V compensatory; he explicitly attributes the old grammars' accentual reading to the most frequent H-L (AB) scheme, i.e. an H on the

sources.quote: Conclusão p.108: 'O quimbundo não possui acento com função distintiva ... essa língua utiliza variações de altura com valor distintivo exclusivamente numa perspectiva paradigmática' (two level tones, A/H and B/L; schemes BB, AA, AB); p.107: vowel-quality change is morphophonological, not 'provocada por questão de acento – inexistente em quimbundo'; p.106: any syllable prominence 'é um fenômeno fonético e muito restrito ... resultado de um espraiamento tonal', the system 'conta exclusivamente com o sistema tonal'. p.84-85: the most frequent word scheme is AB (H on the first of two syllables = p
sources.locator: §3.4 'A Questão Acentual' pp. 101-106; §3.1 p. 84-85 (old grammars' accentual reading rejected); §3.3 p. 98 (syllable-timed rhythm); Conclusão pp. 107-108; §1.5 pp. 5-7 (review of Chatelain and Pedro 1993)
sources.note: Only instrumental/phonological study of Kimbundu prosody; explicitly re-analyses the old grammars' 'penult accent' as the H of the dominant H-L tone scheme and concludes stress is 'inexistente em quimbundo'. Our classification rests solely on Chatelain's 1888 two-line pronunciation note.

sources.quote: 'Accent: General rule: The accent falls on the penult. Ex.: ngitumáka. Exceptions are due: a) to contraction or abscission (kiá from kiabu, bana from banau), b) to foreign origin, especially when the accent falls on the antepenult, c) to enclitic monosyllables, which attract the accent to the last syllable of the preceding word.' / 'Regra geral: O accento tónico recahe sobre a penúltima syllaba.' §192: pairs like -banga/-bánga, njila/njíla differ 'na entoação de toda a palavra ... o accento não é tónico'.
sources.locator: front matter 'Pronunciation' p. xxi-xxii (English) and 'Pronuncia' p. xxii-xxiii (Portuguese); §192 p. 153 (paronym intonation = tone)
